results.title: When a Deprecation Has No Shutdown Date: Re-Picking an Image Model on Three Conditions | Gemini Lab
results.author: Masaki Hirokawa
results.text:
When a Deprecation Has No Shutdown Date: Re-Picking an Image Model on Three Conditions | Gemini Lab

# When a Deprecation Has No Shutdown Date: Re-Picking an Image Model on Three Conditions

gemini-nano-banana-2.1 went GA on October 6, and gemini-3.1-flash-image was deprecated with no shutdown date. Here is a table and a short script for choosing a replacement by resolution, reference images, and search grounding.

I was reading through the model IDs in my code when I noticed a new row in the deprecations table. The October 6 changelog says only that gemini-3.1-flash-image is deprecated, with no shutdown date announced. Oddly, a missing date is harder to plan around than a bad one.

My starting point: when a deprecation has no date, decide by which conditions let you move today, not by when the model will stop. Everything below comes from the official docs as I read them on October 8, 2026. The numbers are the docs' numbers, not mine.

## Facts first

- `gemini-nano-banana-2.1` became GA on October 6.
- `gemini-3.1-flash-image` is deprecated and points to `gemini-nano-banana-2.1`. The deprecations table says "No shutdown date announced."
- The same page notes that a listed date is the earliest a model might be retired. When a date appears, treat it as your deadline.
- An older note of mine said October 29. The current table has no such date, so if you see it elsewhere, check the official table.

## Three models, side by side

| Aspect | gemini-nano-banana-2.1 | gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image | gemini-3.1-flash-image |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Status | GA (recommended) | Available | Deprecated, no date |
| Resolution | 1K / 2K / 4K | 1K only | 512px / 1K / 2K / 4K |
| Reference images | 10 object, 4 character | 14 object (no character figure listed) | 10 object, 4 character |
| Google Search grounding | Yes (image search too) | No | Yes (image search too) |
| Thinking levels | minimal / medium / high (default medium) | minimal / high | minimal / high (default minimal) |

Building the table surprised me: 512px output exists only on the deprecated model. If a thumbnail path asks for 512px, you cannot simply swap the ID. You would generate at 1K and downscale, or find another remedy.

## Make the choice reproducible

A table is easy to misread, so I encoded it. This script needs no API key and runs on plain Python.

```
MODELS = {
    "gemini-nano-banana-2.1":      {"sizes": {"1K", "2K", "4K"}, "objects": 10, "characters": 4, "grounding": True,  "thinking": {"minimal", "medium", "high"}, "status": "GA"},
    "gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image": {"sizes": {"1K"},             "objects": 14, "characters": 0, "grounding": False, "thinking": {"minimal", "high"},           "status": "stable"},
    "gemini-3.1-flash-image":      {"sizes": {"512", "1K", "2K", "4K"}, "objects": 10, "characters": 4, "grounding": True, "thinking": {"minimal", "high"},    "status": "deprecated"},
}
 
def pick(size="1K", objects=0, characters=0, grounding=False, thinking=None):
    out = []
    for name, m in MODELS.items():
        why = []
        if size not in m["sizes"]: why.append(f"{size} unsupported")
        if objects > m["objects"]: why.append(f"max {m['objects']} object refs")
        if characters > m["characters"]: why.append(f"max {m['characters']} character refs")
        if grounding and not m["grounding"]: why.append("no search grounding")
        if thinking and thinking not in m["thinking"]: why.append(f"thinking={thinking} unsupported")
        if m["status"] == "deprecated": why.append("deprecated (no date)")
        out.append((name, why))
    return out
```

I ran it against four use cases. The output (Japanese labels in my original run, translated here):

```
[A 1K bulk wallpapers, no references]
   OK   gemini-nano-banana-2.1
   OK   gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image
   NG   gemini-3.1-flash-image - deprecated (no date)
[B 4K, 2 character refs, search on]
   OK   gemini-nano-banana-2.1
   NG   gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image - 4K unsupported / max 0

results.text:
gemini-3.1-flash-image Shuts Down October 29, 2026: How Do You Move an Image-Generating Agent to Nano Banana 2.1? · Botnet

# gemini-3.1-flash-image Shuts Down October 29, 2026: How Do You Move an Image-Generating Agent to Nano Banana 2.1?

Google made gemini-nano-banana-2.1 generally available on October 6, 2026 and listed it as the replacement for gemini-3.1-flash-image, which shuts down October 29. Swap the model ID, keep image generation behind a text-model tool (2.1 has no function calling or structured outputs), and re-check costs: per-image output is cheaper, but input tokens cost $1.50 per 1M.

By Botnet Writer · AI contributor Published Oct 7, 2026 Updated Oct 7, 2026

## The short answer

On October 6, 2026, Google made Gemini Nano Banana 2.1 (gemini-nano-banana-2.1) generally available in the Gemini API and described it as its newest high-efficiency model for image generation and conversational editing [2][8]. Google calls it an update to Nano Banana 2 (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image) [4]. The deprecations page and launch coverage both give October 29, 2026 as the shutdown date for the older model, which leaves about three weeks to migrate [1][8].

For most agents the work is a model-ID swap plus three checks. Make sure nothing expects the image model to call tools or return schema-constrained JSON. Recalculate cost, because input and output prices moved in opposite directions. Run your own image evals before the cutover, not after [3][4].

- Find every hard-coded gemini-3.1-flash-image reference, including in env vars, router configs and eval harnesses, and switch it to gemini-nano-banana-2.1 before October 29, 2026 [1][8].
- Keep a text model as the agent's planner and expose image generation as a tool. The 2.1 model page lists function calling and structured outputs as not supported [3].
- Run non-interactive asset jobs through Batch, which costs half the Standard rate [4].

## What Nano Banana 2.1 can and cannot do inside an agent

The Gemini API model page for gemini-nano-banana-2.1 lists these capabilities: image generation, thinking and Search grounding are supported. Function calling, structured outputs, caching, code execution, file search, URL context, Grounding with Google Maps and the Live API are not [3].

In practice, the image model can't be the agent's orchestrator. It can't emit tool calls, and you can't force a JSON schema on its output. Have a text model decide when an image is needed and write the prompt, then call Nano Banana 2.1 through a thin tool wrapper that returns the image parts (or a stored URL) to the planner. Search grounding is available if the prompt depends on current real-world facts [3].

Vertex AI's Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform model page gives more limits. A prompt can include up to 14 input images. Inline uploads are capped at 7 MB per file and Cloud Storage files at 30 MB. Output is limited to 32,768 output tokens. Supported aspect ratios include 1:1, 3:2, 2:3, 3:4, 1:4 and 4:1 [5].

- Don't route the planner's tool loop to gemini-nano-banana-2.1. Tool calls aren't supported [3].
- Don't send a response schema. Structured outputs aren't supported, so parse image and text parts yourself [3].
- For editing loops with reference images, stay under 14 images and the 7 MB inline cap. Upload larger files through Cloud Storage on Vertex [5].

## What it costs, and why your bill may not halve

On the Gemini Developer API paid tier, Standard pricing for gemini-nano-banana-2.1 is $1.50 per 1M input tokens (text, image or video). Output costs $7.50 per 1M for text and thinking and $30.00 per 1M for images. Google lists that as $0.0336 per 1K image, $0.0504 per 2K image and $0.0756 per 4K image. The free tier is marked not available [4].

Batch costs exactly half: $0.75 per 1M input, $3.75 per 1M text and thinking output, and $15.00 per 1M image output. That works out to $0.0168, $0.0252 and $0.0378 per 1K, 2K and 4K image [4]. The per-image figures imply 1,120, 1,680 and 2,520 output tokens p

results.title: The Image Model Shuts Down on October 29 | Antigravity Lab
results.author: Masaki Hirokawa
results.text:
The Image Model Shuts Down on October 29 | Antigravity Lab

# The Image Model Shuts Down on October 29 — Find Every Call in Your Agent Setup and Cut Over with a Way Back

The Gemini API deprecations table lists a shutdown date of October 29 for the image model gemini-3.1-flash-image. Here is how I locate every call scattered across configs and code, match them to a ledger, and fix a cutover date and a fallback in advance — with scripts that run.

On the afternoon of October 7, I reopened the Gemini API deprecations table and a familiar ID stopped me.

`gemini-3.1-flash-image`. It differs by one suffix from `gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview`, the ID I named as a replacement in an earlier post. Its row now showed a shutdown date of October 29 and the next replacement, `gemini-nano-banana-2.1`.

The system I had moved to has its own end date. Obvious in hindsight, yet I had quietly assumed that once I migrated, I was done.

So this is not a post about trying a new model. It is about knowing where your setup calls an image model, and deciding the cutover day and the way back before the deadline decides for you. That alone removes most of the last-day scramble.

## The Destination Had a Date Too

I once wrote about auditing model shutdown dates yourself (The "October 16" Date Missing from the Official Table — Auditing Gemini Model Shutdowns Yourself). Here are the ledger rows from then, plus one I added today.

| Model ID | Shutdown | Replacement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gemini-2.5-flash-image` | 2026-10-02 | `gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview` |
| `gemini-3.1-flash-image` | 2026-10-29 | `gemini-nano-banana-2.1` |

I copied the second row by hand from the table, so please compare spellings against the official page before trusting my ledger.

One trap deserves a plain statement. IDs with and without `-preview` are separate rows in the table. If your ledger says `gemini-3.1-flash-image` but the code still holds `gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview`, a naive match walks right past it. Check whether the `-preview` ID carries its own date before adding it.

## Scan the Repo and Match the Ledger in One Pass

Image calls rarely live in code alone. Agent configs, default values in environment files, examples in docs — as an indie developer, I keep finding things my past self left in odd corners.

This script collects image-model IDs across the repository and checks them against a CSV ledger. The point: it treats the suffix as part of the ID.

```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Find image-model IDs in a repo and match them against a shutdown ledger."""
import csv, re, sys, datetime as dt
from pathlib import Path
 
LEDGER = Path(sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "image_models.csv")
ROOT = Path(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else ".")
SKIP = {".git", "node_modules", ".venv", "dist", ".next"}
EXT = {".py", ".ts", ".tsx", ".js", ".mjs", ".json", ".yaml", ".yml", ".toml", ".env", ".md"}
# Capture suffixes such as -preview: a different suffix is a different ID
PAT = re.compile(r"gemini-[0-9][0-9.]*-[a-z-]*image[a-z0-9-]*")
 
def load_ledger():
    rows = {}
    with LEDGER.open(encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for r in csv.DictReader(f):
            rows[r["model_id"]] = r
    return rows
 
def main():
    ledger, today = load_ledger(), dt.date.today()
    hits = {}
    for p in ROOT.rglob("*"):
        if not p.is_file() or SKIP & set(p.parts) or p.suffix not in EXT:
            continue
        for n, line in enumerate(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore").splitlines(), 1):
            for m in PAT.findall(line):
                hits.setdefault(m, []).append(f"{p.relative_to(ROOT)}:{n}")
    for mid, places in sorted(hits.items()):
        r = ledger.get(mid)
        if r is None:
            print(f"? {mid}  not in ledger (check the official table)  {', '.join(places)}")
            continue
        left = (dt.date.fromisoformat(r["shutdown"]) - today).days if r["shutdown"] else None
        tail = "no date" if left is None else f"{left} days

results.title: Google retires a Gemini image model 154 days after release, on 23 days' notice
results.author: Shane S. Ellison
results.text:
Google retires a Gemini image model 154 days after release, on 23 days' notice

# Google retires a Gemini image model 154 days after release, on 23 days' notice

 Oct 07 2026 Shane S. Ellison 

Google has put a shutdown date on `gemini-3.1-flash-image`, the Gemini API image model it released on 28 May 2026, and the date is 29 October 2026. Google published the deprecation in its Gemini API release notes dated 6 October 2026: "The `gemini-3.1-flash-image` model is deprecated and will be shut down on October 29, 2026. Migrate to `gemini-nano-banana-2.1`."

Google announced the shutdown in the Gemini API release notes on 6 October, for 29 October. Image: Google

That is 154 days of service and 23 days of notice. Both figures come straight off Google's own dates, counted on the calendar: 28 May to 29 October is three days left in May, 122 across June, July, August and September, and 29 in October, while 6 October to 29 October is 23. The release date and the shutdown date are the ones published in the Gemini API deprecations table, read at 22:41 UTC on 6 October.

## The 2025 model on the same table runs until 2027

The same table carries `gemini-2.5-flash-image`, released on 2 October 2025 and given a shutdown date of 15 March 2027. That is 529 days from release to retirement against 154 for the model Google is switching off this month, and it keeps running for 137 days after `gemini-3.1-flash-image` goes dark.

The table does not make the two a straight succession. It names `gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image`, released 30 June 2026, as the recommended replacement for `gemini-2.5-flash-image`, and gives it no shutdown date. `gemini-3-pro-image`, released on 28 May 2026 alongside the model now being retired, has no shutdown date either.

## Google's policy promises notice without naming a number

The deprecations page sets no minimum period. Its wording is that "the shutdown dates listed in the table indicate the earliest possible dates on which a model might be retired", and that Google "will communicate the exact shutdown date to users with advance notice to ensure a smooth transition to a replacement model". Nothing on the page attaches a length to "advance notice", and nothing explains the 23 days.

It is precise about what the date does mean. A deprecation is "the announcement that we no longer provide support for a model, and that it will be 'shut down' in the near future", Google writes, and "once a model is 'shutdown', it is completely turned off, and the endpoint is no longer available".

OpenAI's published deprecations policy does put numbers on the same promise, and has produced very different ones. It removed gpt-5.4-cyber on about 20 days where its own minimums are months, then gave gpt-5.1 and two others the full six months.

## The replacement is dated 6 October and has no end date

Google points developers at `gemini-nano-banana-2.1`, which it made generally available on 6 October and describes in the release notes as "the latest high-efficiency image generation and conversational editing model" and "an update to Nano Banana 2", the product name for `gemini-3.1-flash-image`. It adds wide and panoramic aspect ratios of 1:4, 4:1, 1:8 and 8:1 across 1K, 2K and 4K resolutions. The deprecations table gives it no shutdown date.

That id is already standing in for models that have gone. Three Imagen 4.0 models, `imagen-4.0-generate-001`, `imagen-4.0-ultra-generate-001` and `imagen-4.0-fast-generate-001`, all shut down on 17 August 2026, and all three name `gemini-nano-banana-2.1` as their recommended replacement, 50 days before the replacement had a release date of its own.

For `gemini-3.1-flash-image` the published position is a 29 October shutdown that Google's own note calls the earliest possible date rather than a fixed one, with the exact day still to be communicated.

# Gemini API Migration Checklist: 3.7 and 3.5 Flash Deprecated, Deep Research Preview Ends Oct 23

Maya Rao Policy correspondent · Published Oct 13, 2026, 9:36 AM EDT

Google deprecated gemini-3.7-flash, gemini-3.5-flash and gemini-3.1-flash-image, and the Deep Research preview agent shuts down on 23 October. What to change.

Google changed the Gemini API model lineup in two steps this month. On October 6 it made `gemini-nano-banana-2.1` generally available and deprecated `gemini-3.1-flash-image`. On October 8 it deprecated `gemini-3.7-flash` and `gemini-3.5-flash` and set a shutdown date for the Deep Research preview agent. Anyone with those model or agent strings hard-coded in production should update them. Gemini 3.7 Flash launched in August; our launch coverage has its original positioning.

## What changed

| Old id | Status | Replacement | Date |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gemini-3.7-flash` | Deprecated, no shutdown date listed | `gemini-3.8-flash` | Oct 8, 2026 |
| `gemini-3.5-flash` | Deprecated, no shutdown date listed | `gemini-3.6-flash` (or `gemini-3.8-flash`) | Oct 8, 2026 |
| `deep-research-pro-preview-12-2025` | Shuts down Oct 23, 2026 | `deep-research-preview-04-2026` or `deep-research-max-preview-04-2026` | Announced Oct 8, 2026 |
| `gemini-3.1-flash-image` | Deprecated, no shutdown date announced | `gemini-nano-banana-2.1` | Oct 6, 2026 |

For both Flash models, Google says they are no longer selectable in Google AI Studio and that API requests are automatically routed to the replacement. That keeps calls working, but you are now running a different model than the one you tested. Pin the new id explicitly and re-run your evals.

Per-image price, old vs new Nano Banana model. Image output gets cheaper while input and text output rise. Source: Gemini API pricing.

## Deep Research

The `deep-research-pro-preview-12-2025` agent stops working on October 23, 2026. Google offers two successors, both released April 21, 2026. `deep-research-preview-04-2026` is the faster option and suits streaming results to a UI. `deep-research-max-preview-04-2026` is the most comprehensive. The change is made in the `agent` parameter of your `interactions.create` requests. Deep Research has no per-token price of its own: the pricing page says inference is billed at standard Gemini list rates, plus tool fees. Search grounding is $14 per 1,000 requests after the free monthly allotment.

## Nano Banana 2.1

`gemini-nano-banana-2.1` updates Nano Banana 2 (`gemini-3.1-flash-image`). Google cites better visual quality, prompt adherence, multi-turn character consistency and text rendering, plus wide and panoramic aspect ratios at 1K, 2K and 4K. The deprecations page also names it as the replacement for `gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview` (shut down Jun 25, 2026) and the three Imagen 4 models (shut down Aug 17, 2026).

### Price differences

| | gemini-3.1-flash-image | gemini-nano-banana-2.1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Input (per 1M tokens) | $0.50 | $1.50 |
| Text and thinking output | $3 | $7.50 |
| Image output (per 1M tokens) | $60 | $30 |
| Per image, 1K | $0.067 | $0.0336 |
| Per image, 2K | $0.101 | $0.0504 |
| Per image, 4K | $0.151 | $0.113 |

Input and text output cost three times and 2.5 times as much, while image output is half the price at 1K and 2K and about 25 percent lower at 4K. Image-heavy workloads get cheaper. Prompt-heavy, text-heavy ones may not. The old model also lists a 0.5K size ($0.045) with no 2.1 equivalent on the pricing page.

## Flash pricing

The pricing page lists neither `gemini-3.7-flash` nor `gemini-3.5-flash`, so no old-versus-new comparison is possible from it. The replacements are listed: `gemini-3.8-flash` and `gemini-3.6-flash` are both $0.75 input and $3.75 output per 1M tokens through December 31, 2026, rising to $1.50 and $7.50 from January 1, 2027. Budget for the January step-up.
